title_youtube: Face Mites Are Living on Your Face Right Now (They Mate at Night) 🔬
description_youtube:
Face mites live on almost every adult's face: tiny 8-legged Demodex mites, about 0.3 mm long, living head-down inside your pores and hair follicles.

What they actually do:
- They eat the oil (sebum) your skin makes.
- At night they crawl out of the pores to find a mate, then go back in.
- Their genome is so reduced they can't make their own melatonin, so they use the melatonin your skin releases at dusk to stay active all night (Molecular Biology and Evolution, 2022).
- For years scientists thought they had no anus. The 2022 study found one.
- They're normal and mostly harmless. Some researchers think they may even help keep pores unclogged.

Would you rather not know? Tell us below.

Sources:
- University of Reading (2022), The secret lives of mites in the skin of our faces: https://www.reading.ac.uk/news/2022/Research-News/Secret-lives-of-skin-mites-in-our-faces
- Bangor University (2022), same study: https://www.bangor.ac.uk/news/the-secret-lives-of-mites-in-the-skin-of-our-faces
- ScienceDaily (2022), Human follicular mites: ectoparasites becoming symbionts: https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2022/06/220622101404.htm
- National Geographic, Hundreds of tiny arachnids are likely on your face right now: https://www.nationalgeographic.com/premium/article/face-mites-arachnids-human-skin-pores
